item.title: Follow a reporter’s correction about food waste
item.summary: A radio presenter explains why a striking number needed a narrower label.
item.transcript_text: Yesterday I said the college dining hall cut its food waste by a quarter. The figure was accurate for food returned on plates, but I described it too broadly. The dining hall measured how much edible food people left after lunch. It did not include food left in serving trays or food taken away in unopened packs. The team wants to measure those separately next month. Some listeners have asked whether a smaller portion led to more trips to the snack machine. The current data don't tell us. We can report the drop in plate waste and ask whether any changes were displaced elsewhere.

questions.prompt: Why is the presenter speaking now?
options: To retract the measurement as invented
To announce that the hall is closing
To correct the way a figure was described
To tell listeners to eat smaller lunches
questions.explanation: The number stands, but the label attached to it was too broad.

questions.prompt: What did the team actually measure?
options: Every unused ingredient in the building
Edible food left on plates after lunch
The number of unopened packs taken away
Snack sales after lunch
questions.explanation: The measured category was plate waste.

questions.prompt: What will the team consider separately later?
options: Serving-tray leftovers and unopened takeaway packs
The price of every lunch
Kitchen wages and snack costs
Which plates were used each day
questions.explanation: Neither category was included in the original measure.

questions.prompt: How does the presenter treat the snack-machine suggestion?
options: As an established consequence
As something the team ruled out
As the explanation for the entire drop
As possible but unanswered by the current data
questions.explanation: The presenter says the current data do not answer it.

questions.prompt: Which headline accurately describes the result?
options: College food waste fell by a quarter
Unopened packs fell by a quarter
Plate waste at college lunch fell by a quarter
Quarter of students bought snacks instead
questions.explanation: It gives the correct result without widening its scope.
